Checked all four parts.
- (a) The stage texts of GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.4, K.6 and K.7 are classical. K.4 is Waldhausen categories and S_n C. K.6 is 'a nonconnective K-theory spectrum for the enhanced exact/complex categories … One concrete route uses flasque enlargement and suspension'. K.7 is Morita, products and filtered colimits. None mentions stable ∞-categories, Cat_∞^perf, localizing invariants, K of ring spectra, Land–Tamme, truncating invariants, the theorem of the heart, Thomason–Neeman or A-theory. The 'enhanced' categories and the edge E5:abstract → K.4 enter only as hypotheses of comparisons; the K.6 packet's derived-Morita node says 'Neither pinned library has enhanced categories or a K-theory of them, which is recorded here as the reason the node is a comparison and not a construction'.
- (b) Both GAKT packets are accepted (28 September 2026), with every stage in scope 'source_decomposed'. Their sources are Weibel's K-book and Schlichting 2003, and neither contains 'Tamme', '2001.10425', 'localizing' or 'Blumberg'. Their issues (#737, #738) predate the extraction, and make_queue.py adds a source route's paper only to blueprint prompts generated later. So the source route never reached them.
- (c) Route 1's brief says 'Import, never re-plan … the spectral and infinity-categorical extensions this paper's extraction routes into K.4, K.6 and K.7'. The review's route 1 reason also credits K.1–K.7 with 'the universal localizing-invariant interfaces'.
- (d) CM21/127 is planned at K.6, RT.2 and RT.3; CM21/128–/130 are on a route its review rejected; and CMM21/074 (Land–Tamme excision) is on CMM21's accepted source route to RT.3.
A search of every stage text for these notions finds no other owner. RT.5 ('localizing motives … from enhanced small stable categories') is a consumer that assumes the parent supplies them, and H.5 disclaims a universal characterisation of localizing invariants. High is right: nothing plans the twelve foundational items, and every theorem of the Part II rests on them.
The fix's direction is right: make_queue.paper_designs merges every Part II proposal for the parent into the single job DESIGN-GeneralAlgebraicKTheoryPartII, which is a sensible shared owner. It needs one frontier condition. The new first layer has consumers that the Part II itself imports: CMM21/074 at RT.3 (accepted), RT.5, and CM21/127. So the brief must make that layer import only EnhancedDerivedSheaves E0/E5, StableHomotopyKTheory H.3/H.5 and GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.1–K.6, not RT.2/RT.3, so that RT.3 and RT.5 can import it without a cycle. /32 should coalesce with CMM21/074. The maintainer should know that RT.3's accepted Land–Tamme item then imports this layer. Otherwise as proposed: move the twelve items to route 1, delete route 3, replace the 'Import, never re-plan' clause with imports of what K.2:plus/H.3, K.3/devissage-theorem, K.4, K.5 and K.6 do plan, and correct the report's §Routing and the review's route 1 and route 3 reasons.

Checked. Item /48 reads 'For a T(n)-local spectrum X the Tate construction X^{tC_p} vanishes; consequently (L_n^{p,f}S)^{tC_p} is an algebra over L_{n−1}^{p,f}S', and route 2's brief lists 'Kuhn's blueshift theorem for the Tate construction' among its final theorems. The paper states only the second clause: Remark 3.9, p. 16, 'The spectrum (L_n^{p,f}S)^{tC_p} is itself an algebra over L_{n−1}^{p,f}S by Kuhn's blueshift result [Kuh04]'. CMNN quote Kuhn correctly: 'if a spectrum X is L_n^{p,f}-local then X^{tC_p} is L_{n−1}^{p,f}-local' (arXiv:2011.08233v2, p. 3), and 'Tate constructions vanish in T(i)-local homotopy' (p. 16).
The counterexample holds. KU_p^∧ with trivial C_p-action is K(1)-local, hence T(1)-local. For complex-oriented E, π_*E^{tC_p} = E^*((x))/[p]_F(x), and for KU_p^∧, [p](t) = (1 + t)^p − 1 = t·Φ_p(1 + t), so π_0 = Z_p((t))/Φ_p(1 + t) = Q_p(ζ_p) ≠ 0. This spectrum is rational, hence T(1)-acyclic, as Kuhn's theorem predicts. High is right: /48 is the formulation the design job receives for a named final theorem, and it is false.
Adjustment to the fix: the proposed restatement drops Kuhn's hypothesis in its first clause. 'For a finite group G and a spectrum X with G-action, L_{T(n)}(X^{tG}) = 0' is false without 'X T(n)-local'. For X = S with trivial C_p-action, the Segal conjecture for C_p (Lin, Gunawardena; Nikolaus–Scholze Thm III.1.7) gives S^{tC_p} ≃ S_p^∧, and L_{T(n)}(S_p^∧) = L_{T(n)}S ≠ 0 for n ≥ 1. Restate /48 as: 'Kuhn [Kuh04]: for a finite group G and a T(n)-local spectrum X with G-action, L_{T(n)}(X^{tG}) = 0, equivalently the T(n)-local norm L_{T(n)}(X_{hG}) → X^{hG} is an equivalence; in blueshift form, if X is L_n^{p,f}-local then X^{tC_p} is L_{n−1}^{p,f}-local, so (L_n^{p,f}S)^{tC_p} is an algebra over L_{n−1}^{p,f}S. The Tate construction itself need not vanish: (KU_p^∧)^{tC_p} has π_0 = Q_p(ζ_p).' Use the same formulation in the route 2 brief.

Checked. PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-21 was merged on 22 September 2026 (#1990), before this extraction (#2209, 23 September). Its /118 ('Chromatic localizations: L_1, L_{K(1)}, L_n^f, Morava K-theory and telescopes', with 'T(0) = HQ' and 'L_n^f : Sp → Sp_(p) is p-localization followed by finite localization'), /150, /024 and /142 sit on its route to MotivicEtaleKTheoryPartIISelmerAndEtaleKTheory. REV-PAPER-CLAUSEN-MATHEW-21 rejected that route because 'generic chromatic/equivariant spectra … must be supplied by their owning roadmaps'. So the revision of CM21 needs an owner, and ChromaticHomotopyTheory is the natural one. Neither this extraction's report nor its review mentions CM21. The conventions clash: LMMT §2.1, p. 6, 'We adopt the convention that T(0) = S[1/p]' (/16), against CM21's T(0) = HQ. These have different Bousfield classes, since S[1/p] ⊗ S/ℓ ≠ 0 for a prime ℓ ≠ p. Medium is right.
Two precisions to the fix:
- (a) The two L_n^f agree. LMMT's L_n^f localizes at the p-local HQ ⊕ T(1) ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ T(n) (/20), which is CM21's p-localization followed by finite localization. The incompatibility is only the symbol T(0) and the non-p-local L_n^{p,f}. One convention for T(0), with /24 as the comparison lemma, is the fix.
- (b) Of the CM21 items, only /118 (with the L_1 = L_{KU} it needs) is chromatic basics for ChromaticHomotopyTheory to own. /150 (noncommutative motives), /142 (CMNN descent, see finding 5(h)) and /024 are consumers that belong with their K-theory or motivic owners, importing the chromatic roadmap.

Checked. /82 ('Connective real and complex K-theory and the Bott elements': ko, ku, KO, KU, their Bott elements, ko[1/β] ≃ KO and ku[1/β] ≃ KU) is missing on route 2. The route 2 brief both orders 'connective and periodic real and complex topological K-theory with their Bott elements' constructed and, a paragraph later, imports RefinedTraceMethods RT.4:topological. RT.4:topological reads 'Construct topological complex K-theory from vector bundles, prove Bott periodicity and its spectrum-level multiplication, and define ku as the connective cover of KU. Identify π_*ku=ℤ[β] and π_*KU=ℤ[β,β⁻¹] with |β|=2, proving the localization comparison'. So the complex half is planned, and no stage plans ko, KO or β ∈ π_8 ko. The paper uses both halves (Corollary 4.19 and Remark 4.20, p. 21). The split is frontier-safe, since no atlas stage depends on the new roadmap. Medium is right, and the fix is right. Optionally, the ko/KO item's note cites Tau Ceti SpinRepresentations Layer 7 (Clifford-algebra Bott periodicity) as algebraic input.

No layer plans that half. K.3/devissage-theorem's standing instance is G-theory modulo a nilpotent ideal, not K_0 of projectives. S.5 plans the fundamental theorem for Laurent rings. The KTheoryLowDegrees--U.1 packet says 'Not targets of Z.1 and so not planned here: … nilpotent-ideal invariance (II.2.2)'. Mathlib 082e2d3 has the lifting lemmas exists_isIdempotentElem_eq_of_ker_isNilpotent (RingTheory/Idempotents.lean:249, for noncommutative rings, which idempotent matrices need), OrthogonalIdempotents.lift_of_isNilpotent_ker (:274) and CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents.lift_of_isNilpotent_ker (:325). Adjustment to the fix: split /68 as proposed, but prefer a source route to KTheoryLowDegrees Z.1 for the K_0 half. Cite all three Mathlib lemmas. The negative-degree half stays planned at K.6, as the routine induction from K.6/fundamental-theorem-with-nil-terms and the K_0 half, and its note should say so. The split is necessary, since Z.1 is upstream of K.6.

Checked on 400 dpi page images of pp. 25–26 and against the v5 LaTeX. The preamble loads \usepackage[mathscr]{euscript}, and Euler Script has capital letters only, so the lower-case 'yc' of \mathscr{Cyc} typesets as nothing. The printed subscript in Proposition 4.33 and in Corollary 4.34's first sentence and display is the same glyph with the same spacing (the word boxes agree). The printed paper therefore shows one symbol, 𝒪_𝒞(G), throughout, and E2's 'printed' and 'reason' fields describe the source, not the published text. §18 defines a misprint as a slip in what was read, and a difference no reader can see is not one. The register lists E2 as a confirmed new mistake, so medium is right. One precision: the introduction (p. 5) prints an Euler-script 𝒪 where §4 prints a calligraphic 𝒪, so 'the same letter' holds for the subscript 𝒞, not the whole symbol. The fix is right: E2's review becomes 'rejected', /99 writes 𝒪_𝒞(G), and the report's and the review's E2 paragraphs are corrected.

Checked. LMMT Remark 3.9 (p. 16): 'Theorem I.3.3ii and an analogue of Lemma I.3.8iii from [NS18] imply that End_𝒬(R) ≃ R^{tC_p}. By Theorem I.3.6 in op. cit., 𝒬 has a canonical symmetric monoidal structure and we obtain a symmetric monoidal functor Perf(R^{tC_p}) → 𝒬.' In the accepted PAPER-NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18, /24 (Theorem I.3.3) and /26 (Theorem I.3.6) are on its accepted source route to EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:abstract/E5:presentability, and /28 (Lemma I.3.8) is at RT.2. /49 routes material resting on them to RT.2/RT.3 with no pointer to that owner. Low is right.
The fix needs narrowing. /49's statement is already the application to this particular 𝒬 (End_𝒬(R) ≃ R^{tC_p}, the canonical symmetric monoidal structure on 𝒬, the functor Perf(R^{tC_p}) → 𝒬, K(𝒬) a K(R^{tC_p})-module); it does not restate I.3.3 or I.3.6 in general. So the double ownership is in the locator, not the statement. Keep the statement, since the red team's restricted wording would drop the functor Perf(R^{tC_p}) → 𝒬 that makes K(𝒬) a module. An item cannot be 'imported' by status, so add a note instead: Theorems I.3.3 and I.3.6 are NS18 /24 and /26 at E5:abstract/E5:presentability, and Lemma I.3.8 is its /28 at RT.2, and the RT design imports them and plans only this application. The edge is acyclic: E5:abstract is upstream of RT.2 and RT.3, and E5:presentability is incomparable with them.

Checked. (1) p. 23, the sentence after Corollary 4.23: 'In the case of HZ-algebras, the last assertion of Corollary 4.30 also appears in [BCM20]'. The source has \Cref{compKTC} there, and compKTC is Corollary 4.30, the height n ≥ 2 comparison L_{T(n)}K(A) = L_{T(n)}K(τ_{≥0}A) = L_{T(n)}TC(τ_{≥0}A). BCM20 is a height-1 result, and §1 says the height-1 statement 'recovers the result of Bhatt–Clausen–Mathew [BCM20] for HZ-algebras'. So the last assertion of Corollary 4.23, L_{K(1)}K(A) = L_{K(1)}K(A[1/p]), is meant. The v4 source has the same slip. (2) Remark 3.9, p. 15: '[CMNN23, Lemma 4.5]'. The bibliography cites [CMNN23] unversioned, as arXiv:2011.08233. In v2 (8 November 2022), current when LMMT v5 appeared, the statement is Theorem 4.6, and 4.5 is Remark 4.5 on assembly maps. Lemma 4.5 is v1's numbering, which LMMT v4 cited correctly when written. Low is right. Adjustment: scope E4's correction to arXiv:2011.08233v2 (the published Annales numbering was not checked), and say that the citation matched v1.

Checked. /1 states E_1-rings as algebras in the symmetric monoidal ∞-category Sp, RMod(R) and X ⊗ Y = X ⊗ Σ^∞Y. It is planned at StableHomotopyKTheory H.5:spectra and EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:abstract and E5:presentability, and its note says 'Nothing in the atlas fixes the smash product of a spectrum with a pointed space'. Adjustment to the fix: add E5:spectra-comparison to /1's planned list, but not H.5:S-delooping. After RS-33 the generic smash product is planned at H.5:spectra, which the list already has, and H.5:S-delooping only reexports it. Replace the note's false sentence with that account.

Checked. The arXiv API gives journal_ref 'J. Amer. Math. Soc. 37 (2024), 1011-1040'. Crossref's record for 10.1090/jams/1043 still has no volume, issue or pages, and no update relation. The AMS article PDF was not served to this verifier either. So the published text is unread, and the findings stay against arXiv v5. The file's venue lacks the page range, readSections[3] is out of date, and there is no sourceVersions list. Low is right.
The proposed sourceVersions is wrong in one part. scripts/collation.py's provenance() returns 'published' as soon as any sourceVersions entry has kind 'published', whatever its url or citation says. Tested on this file: with the red team's two entries provenance becomes 'published', and with the preprint entry alone it stays 'preprint'. A 'published' entry for a text that was not read would tell collation that the findings were checked against the version of record, the opposite of the truth. Set the venue to 'Journal of the American Mathematical Society 37 (2024), no. 4, 1011–1040' and add only the preprint entry: kind 'preprint', url https://arxiv.org/pdf/2001.10425v5, read 2026-09-23, sha256 9eabee34…40baa2f, with a note that the published text was not served and the findings are scoped to v5.
